newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany says NATO not considering move to Bonn.
newsitem.headline: Germany says NATO not considering move to Bonn.

text.p: Germany said on Wednesday it knew of no plans to move NATO headquarters from Brussels to Bonn but would welcome international institutions to the city after the German government moves to Berlin.

"The government assumes NATO will keep its headquarters in Brussels. The government has not heard of any deliberations about moving NATO to Bonn," government spokesman Herbert Schmuelling told a news conference.

Bonn's General-Anzeiger daily on Wednesday quoted "informed sources" in Brussels as saying NATO was considering moving its headquarters, possibly to Bonn, to mark its new eastern orientation as it welcomed new members to the group.
Such a move, of only about 250 km (150 miles) eastwards, would have a "symbolic character", the newspaper said.

Schmuelling said NATO was considering how much space it would need as the organisation expanded and a questionnaire on the topic had been circulated to members, but he thought the alliance would expand in and around Brussels.

The 16-nation alliance is due to meet in Madrid in July to invite an advance guard of former communist foes from eastern Europe to open membership talks. Leading the long list of candidates are Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic.
Schmuelling said the German government would be very pleased if international authorities came to Bonn, but added the chances of NATO coming here were slim.
"Bonn is very interested in international authorities because of rooms and halls becoming free with most of the government moving from Bonn to Berlin," he said.
The government is due to move most of its ministries to Berlin, the German capital, by 1999.
